chunks: MOSFET use cases. The question: What are some use cases of a MOSFET?
A MOSFET is a voltage-controlled switch or valve, and it is used in three big places.
It switches power on and off, it forms the logic gates (the tiny yes/no decision circuits) inside every chip, and it works as an amplifier or adjustable resistor in analog circuits.
It is popular because a tiny voltage on its insulated gate controls a lot of current.
Think of a light switch that needs no effort to hold. You flick it with a voltage, and it stays on without you pushing.
A small signal from a microcontroller flips the switch for something large, like a motor. Billions of these tiny switches, wired in pairs, make up a processor.
Sorting by operating region explains the "why."
Switches flip between cutoff and triode, amplifiers and current sources sit in saturation, and analog switches use triode as a variable resistor.
Switch: a part that is either fully on or fully off. Gate drive: the voltage and current you supply to the gate to turn the MOSFET on or off.
Low-side switch: a switch between the load and ground. CMOS: logic built from paired N-channel and P-channel MOSFETs.
R DS(on) : the resistance between drain and source when the MOSFET is fully on.
A 3. 3 volts microcontroller pin cannot power a 12 volts motor directly. Put an NFET between the motor and ground, and connect the pin to its gate.
Pin high turns the NFET on, and the motor runs. Say the motor draws 1 amps and the NFET has 10 milliohms of R DS(on) : it drops 1 times 0. 01 equals 0. 01 volts and wastes only 0.
01 watts. That is the whole idea.
"Three main areas.
Switching: low-side NFETs driving motors, relays and LEDs from a GPIO, PFET high-side load switches, and the switches in buck converters, H-bridges and synchronous rectifiers.
Digital: every CMOS gate and memory cell.

Analog: in saturation it's a voltage-controlled current source for amplifiers, current mirrors and LDO pass elements, and in triode it's a voltage-controlled resistor for analog switches and level shifters.
The insulated gate and low on-resistance are why it fits all of them."
